Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

energyRt 0.90.0 (pre-release)

The first release since 0.50-beta. It consolidates the 0.60, 0.70 and 0.80 development cycles, none of which were released, and is the pre-release for 1.0: the modelling API is the one 1.0 will ship, and the work left is testing, debugging and visualisation rather than new structure.

Upgrading from 0.50 is not a drop-in. The time dimension, the storage class, the variant system and the geography layer all changed shape — read Breaking changes first. The change-by-change log for the whole cycle (450 entries) is in dev/NEWS-0.6-0.9-detail.md.

License

  • energyRt is relicensed from AGPL-3 to Apache-2.0. Releases up to and including v0.89 remain available under AGPL-3.

Breaking changes

  • The time dimension is timeslice everywhere (was slice), matching TIMES and OSeMOSYS, and a calendar is required wherever a timeslice layout is needed. Timeslice label conversion moved to the sibling timescales package, so tsl2hour(), tsl2year(), tsl_guess_format() and tsl_formats are gone. calendars ships generic designs (m12, q4, d365_h24, sampled variants); model-specific ones live with their models.

  • A storage is three parts. Charger, reservoir and discharger each have their own capacity variable, costs and availability: @input/@output/ @storage declare the roles, vStorageOutCap/vStorageInpCap/ vStorageStgCap size them, @duration and @inp2out/@inp2stg tie them together, and vStorageStore is now vStorageLevel. Charge and discharge rates are bounded by the converters: inp.af.up/out.af.up default to 1, so a flow per timeslice cannot exceed capacity * cap2act * share.

  • Vintages and clusters are one mechanism. @vintage holds build years (with the investment window merged in from @start/@end/@olife) and @cluster holds parallel parts; both must be declared before a label may be used in a data slot, and interpolation expands them into ordinary processes named EWIN_VIN2030_CL01. Read coordinates from getVariants(), never by parsing a name.

  • Geography is multi-level. @geolevel is @geoframe on commodities and summands, a model carries a Geoscale (from the sibling geoscales package), and a commodity or process may sit at a coarser level than the flows it touches.

  • Taxes and subsidies are indexed by the instrument, not by the commodity, and can be levied on a process. newConstraintS() is removed — it failed for every input it was given; declare a constraint or a levy instead.

  • Auxiliary flows sit at the aux commodity’s timeframe: an annual emission of an hourly plant is one variable and one equation per year, not 8760. The storage aux couplings are part-prefixed (inp.cap2ainp, stg.ncap2aout, …); the bare names silently applied to the discharger only.

  • The API is verb-first and prefixed en: scenario management reads save_scenario() / load_scenario() / drop_scenario_run(), the registry class is en_registry, and 46 machinery helpers are no longer exported. Object names are validated at construction. The 0.5-era deprecation layer is gone: storage@charge/@inflow and the slice column name are refused with an error naming the new spelling, and the un-prefixed solver path environment variables and options(energyRt.verbose) are no longer read.

  • The Julia and Python backends exchange Arrow files, which needs Arrow.jl and pyarrow; arrow_format split into storage_format and exchange_format. A run’s solver files are written into runs/<solve>/.

  • The teaching model is TOPIA (was UTOPIA), its regions are W1/W2, C1–C6, E1–E3, and its four standalone datasets are folded into topia. The test tier nightly is renamed full.

  • The first argument is object wherever a function takes an energyRt object: 66 functions that said obj, mod or scen now say object (getData(), interpolate_model(), solve_model() and the solve drivers, the scenario-store verbs, get_process_*(), …). Positional calls are unaffected; a call naming the argument (getData(scen = s)) must be updated. x stays where the argument is data rather than a model object, and generics defined elsewhere (summary(), autoplot(), update()) keep their formals.

  • storage@cap2stg is refused rather than renamed: it became @duration in 0.80, and the compatibility shim is gone. The error names the replacement. storage@charge and @inflow are refused the same way, and the error says why it is not a pure rename: @startLevel is added once per cycle at the first timeslice, where @charge added its value at every timeslice given. For a weather-driven inflow profile, feed the storage from a supply.

  • newSub() is removed — newSubsidy() is the constructor. They were the same function, and newTax() never had a short alias.

New features

Model building

  • Resource tiers in one object. A commodity or a weather object declaring @cluster becomes one object per tier at interpolation, each with its own balance, so graded land or a graded wind resource cannot pool. A consumer picks its tier by cluster name; an unclustered object is untouched.
  • Weather transforms: one shipped series feeds many derived ones, and a weather object may be declared at a coarser region than the processes reading it — one stored profile for a whole country.
  • Transmission: newACLine() and newDCLink(), an opt-in Kirchhoff voltage law, quadratic losses approximated by capacity tranches (lossTranches()), and @trade$af to rate a route’s flow.
  • Supply curves: asSupplyCurve(), asImportCurve(), asExportCurve() turn a single price into a stepped curve with its own roster.
  • commodity@property carries physical properties — heating values, densities, carbon content — as a tidy table rather than scattered coefficients.
  • Discount rates may be declared at any geoscale level, and a WACC per technology is separate from the social discount rate, with payback as the cost-recovery life on every backend.
  • Process definitions are portable: process_to_spec() / process_from_spec() (YAML/JSON), an interactive process_designer(), and Excel round-trip with read_technology_xlsx() / write_technology_xlsx().

Time and space

  • Irregular calendars. A parent may have any number of children, so a calendar can nest the days of the year under months of 28-31 days. A timeslice is named by the shortest unique part of its path (m01, d001, d001_h00); regular calendars are built as before. A hand-built sample for solve_by_sample() no longer has to be a complete cross and keeps the full calendar’s names. A timetable whose rows are out of time order is refused. New calendars m12_d365_h24 and m12_d365_h24_1dpm put months above the days of d365_h24.
  • Calendars gained year_start and utc_offset_minutes, milestone years can carry display labels, and sampled calendars (one representative day per month, d365_h24_1dps) are first-class — a full model solved on a subset of slices.
  • Region aggregation with clustering: aggregate_model_regions(clusters = ) partitions a corridor family into k groups, get_process_groups() reports what may be merged, process_cluster_sweep() sweeps the admissible range and model_clusters() reports what an aggregation did.
  • A filtered geoscale passed to interpolate_model() solves a sub-territory, and subset_model_regions() warns when sampling splits a cell a process spans.
  • Auxiliary flows on a coarse process. A technology or storage declared at a region coarser than an auxiliary commodity it draws or emits now holds that flow in every finer cell beneath it: the aux variables sit at the commodity’s own regions while the coupling stays at the process’s cell, and the equation sums the children. A per-region limit on the aux commodity therefore binds without splitting the process per region. Previously any @aux / @aeff row made a process ineligible to be coarse at all.
  • @geoframe on the region-carrying classes (weather, supply, demand, technology, storage, import, export, tax, subsidy, trade) declares the geoscale level an object’s regions are expressed at. Optional: left unset the level is derived from the region codes, as before. Declared, it scopes an object that names no regions of its own to that level’s regions, and every code it does name must be a member of the level — geoframe = "nation" beside region = "R1" is now an error instead of quietly meaning something else. It adds that one default and those checks, nothing more: an object may still be coarser only than the commodities it consumes, never than those it produces or stores, enforced where it always was.

Solving

  • Solve drivers: solve_myopic() (window by window, with a solution ledger), solve_by_sample(), solve_by_region() and solve_guided() (target-seeking), each with its primitives exported.
  • GPU and first-order LP: presets for cuOpt (julia_cuopt, mm_cuopt_wsl) and HiGHS PDLP/HiPDLP, plus lang = "mm", which hands the matrix to multimod and solves it outside the templates.
  • solver_options$pyomo_mps writes the problem as MPS, and read_solution() reads a solution produced outside energyRt.
  • en_check_solve() solves a tiny model on every configured backend and reports what actually works; en_check_packages() / en_install_deps() / en_install_julia_pkgs() set the toolchains up.
  • interpolate_model() is about 6x faster on large models, folds year as well as region and timeslice, and logs its per-stage timings. The technology group and share maps are built once per run rather than once per map, and the object loop no longer slows down with the number of objects: a model of 21,000 objects interpolates in about 20 minutes instead of 48.
  • save_scenario() and save_model() keep tables below getOption("energyRt.ondisk_min_rows", 1e5) rows in the object’s .RData instead of writing a file for each; saving a model of many small objects no longer takes tens of minutes.
  • The mm route keeps folded numeric parameters folded when the installed multimod looks wildcards up itself, instead of expanding them on import.
  • Remote solving: the NEOS server for GAMS/CPLEX without a local licence, and GPU execution in the cloud.
  • interpolate_model(fx_equ = TRUE) writes a fixed bound (.fx, or .lo == .up) as one equality row, eq<Family>Fx, instead of a lower and an upper row, in every bound family (availability, shares, capacities, storage, supply, trade, import/export rows): about 25% fewer rows on hourly VRE models, same solution. fx_equ = FALSE keeps the pairs.

Results, storage and sharing

  • A project registry keyed on path records every model, scenario and dataset, with a lifecycle (seal_*() / unseal_*(), mark_delete() / delete_marked()) and summary() reporting counts and staleness. Objects are reachable by name: getScenario("base").
  • Runs and artifacts: scenario_runs(), scenario_solutions() and scenario_artifacts() say what each solve produced and left on disk; promote_solution() and import_solution() choose which one counts; drop_solver_outputs() and drop_scenario_run() clean up.
  • Results live in Arrow stores, so a solution larger than memory stays readable, and getData(run = ) reads several runs in one call.
  • prepare_for_sharing() writes a cleaned, trimmed copy of a stored scenario and strip_user_info() removes the machine it was made on.

Validation

  • validate_scenario_parameters() separates structural findings (the model would solve to a meaningless answer) from advisory ones, and names them: missing flow-to-capacity links (free_meal), constraint tuples with no data behind them, coefficient ranges that will hurt a solver, and variant provenance that disagrees with the process names.

  • verify_solution() re-derives the model’s own identities from the results, with check groups (checks = "all"), and verify_checks() lists them.

  • getVariants() also takes a model, listing the names vintages and clusters will expand to before interpolating.

  • report() on a technology or storage takes spatial and solved context: geoscale = adds a map of where the process is declared, model = prices it in that model’s calendar, horizon and discount, and scenario = adds what the solve realized – capacity built per region, and the ex-post levelized cost beside the ex-ante one, per variant. scenario implies its model, which implies its geoscale; a model that is not the scenario’s is refused.

  • levcost() on a solved scenario accepts a base process name and prices every variant of it, returning the same levcost_variants result the declared-object path gives (by_variant = included). A vector of names works too; variants the solver never built are reported and skipped.

  • audit_coefficients() reports the coefficient range of a written model, per equation.

  • compare_scenarios(), compare_models() and compare_inputs() diff solved results, declarations and interpolated inputs.

Reporting and visualisation

  • report() for every object: 14 element classes plus model and scenario containers, rendered to HTML, PDF, Word or TeX, cached, with user-defined process groups, branding and a report_* helper family for custom templates.

  • Levelized cost: levcost() prices technologies, storages (LCOS) and trade routes (LCOT) analytically — no solver — per vintage, cluster and region, with results cached and plotted by autoplot().

  • draw() sketches a process as a diagram, including a storage’s three parts and its ratio couplings.

  • autoplot() covers objects, calendars, horizons, scenarios and comparisons, with by = "vintage" / "cluster" fan-outs; plot_map(), plot_trade_map() and plot_trade_network() map any solved variable carrying a region.

  • TOPIA is rebuilt around concentrated resources. COA and GAS are balanced per zone and traded between zones (TBD_COA_*, TBD_GAS_*) while electricity trades region to region; the endowments are finite (ava.up), with coal in WEST, gas in EAST, reservoir hydro in C4/E1/C1 and the one nuclear station in C1. A kit model therefore needs its hierarchy – setGeoscale(mod, kit$geoscale) – every process carries a desc, and costs are USD. STG_ELC is respecified: cap2act puts its capacity in the same GW as the technologies, @duration is reservoir energy per unit of power (four hours is 4 * 0.0036 PJ/GW, not 4), and the energy cost moves to stg.invcost, which prices the reservoir.

Deprecations

  • None pending. The 0.5-era deprecation layer and its ?energyRt-deprecated page are removed, and the renames in this cycle are hard breaks: the error names the new spelling.

Bug fixes

Around 130 individual fixes are listed in the detailed log; most changed an answer rather than only the code. The classes worth knowing about:

  • report() without format renders HTML only; model, scenario and comparison reports rendered all four formats.

  • A fixed weather factor fixed nothing. waf.fx (and the storage and supply equivalents) entered only the upper bound unless the process also declared af.lo, so VRE output could fall below the weather and curtailment never reached vBalance. It now binds from both sides.

  • wafs and wafc. wafs multiplies afs: without afs it is now an error, and its weather must have a value at each afs timeslice (a weather at another timeframe read as 0 and shut the technology down). wafc acts like waf at the commodity’s timeframe: with no afc it implies afc = 1 on the sides it sets (it was silently ignored).

  • Parameters that never reached the solver. Several slots were declared but not wired (pTradeIrEff, per-part storage fixom/eac, aux couplings on an unpriced part), so a cost or a limit was silently dropped and the model solved without it.

  • Equations instantiated where no data stood behind them, which made the solver read its own default — a bound of 0 shutting a process down, or an unbounded flow where the user expected a rating.

  • Multi-level geography: emissions of plants in sub-regions are counted, coarse supply keeps its cost, a repeated region code at two adjacent levels no longer poisons its parent, and a geoscale whose levels do not nest is refused rather than silently flattened.

  • Levies and constraints: a levy on a timeslice-indexed base is weighted, taxes survive folding, and a summand’s timeframe / geoframe is resolved per member instead of from the pooled index.

  • Levelized cost: priced variants no longer return NA, a vintage outside the priced horizon is handled, a trade corridor is priced at what the model actually pays, and a repository is priced process by process.

  • Reporting the truth: an infeasible or unbounded model is a result rather than an error, verify_solution() stops double-counting coarse regions, and a non-interactive run no longer stops at a debugger prompt.

  • aeff$cout2ainp and aeff$cinp2aout now bind. Both looked their main commodity up in the wrong flow domain — the output-driven coupling in the input domain and vice versa — so on a process that does not carry the same commodity on both sides the coupling was dropped and the auxiliary flow came out zero. The ratio was in the model inputs, which is why it looked set. Models that declare either coupling will see the auxiliary flow, and its cost, appear.

  • get_process_*(process = ) is honoured. get_process_inputs(), _outputs(), _aux(), _region(), _invest_window() and _timeframe() accepted the argument and ignored it, returning every process in the model; get_process_comm() inherited it. The returned shape was right, so the answer looked right.

  • A weather series whose data omits region is stored where it is declared. pWeather took its regions from the data column while the two weather maps took theirs from @region, so a region-agnostic profile declared at a coarse region was materialised at every region of every geoscale level. No answer moves — every backend reads the series through mWeatherRegionAt — but the parameter no longer claims it where nothing declared it.

  • levcost() could not price a technology whose commodity is balanced at a coarser @geoframe. The screening model carries no hierarchy, so the declaration is now dropped on the way in, as @emis already was.

  • levcost() replicated every availability row into every screening region, so a model pricing one fuel differently by region produced a repeated key and interpolation stopped with “multiplied a series”. Rows are now kept where a region has its own, and collapsed to the cheapest where they name regions (or a coarser level) the screening model does not have.

Documentation

  • A rebuilt pkgdown site with tutorial articles for installation, backends, model bricks, units, time and space resolution, storage, vintages and clusters, the three-part TOPIA walk-through, workflow, scenario management, reports and autoplot().
  • The testing strategy — tiers check < fast < cross < full, the @covers coverage matrix, tracked goldens — is documented in tests/README.md, tests/TESTING.md and the Testing strategy article.
  • ?add, ?read, ?interpolate, ?setCalendar, ?setHorizon, ?getHorizon and ?add_to_convert open a help page. The generics were exported with only their methods documented, so the bare names resolved to nothing.
  • Every public help page has an example. 82 topics had none; they now build what they use, on the shipped TOPIA kits, so each runs as pasted. Examples needing a solver, a project store, pandoc or a python environment are marked \dontrun{} but were executed before being written in.

energyRt 0.50.9-dev

Breaking changes

  • Time-slice weighting is rewritten: variables with a slice dimension are no longer weighted, for consistency between sampled and non-sampled runs. Slice weights can vary across model years.
  • Variables with a year dimension are no longer weighted to interval lengths, except cumulative variables (vSupReserveCum) and capacity variables, which represent the state at the end of the period.
  • New-capacity variables (vTechNewCap) are given per year — apply pPeriodLen to get total new capacity by the end of each period.
  • System costs are regrouped by type (capital, fixed O&M, variable O&M, supply, taxes, subsidies) and by process type, and the Total Costs equation rewritten to match.

Bug fixes

  • optimizeRetirment = TRUE no longer retires new technologies at the same time as their installation.
  • draw() on a trade no longer repeats arrows.
  • newCosts() is debugged, with an example in the Topia tutorial.
  • tsl2hour() identifies n-digit hours; it previously worked for two only.
